newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bourse traded Clariant after news.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bourse traded Clariant after news.

text.p: Trading in Swiss chemicals group Clariant continued for about four minutes after a merger announcement by Hoechst AG on Tuesday before the Swiss exchange suspended trading, officials said on Wednesday.
Bourse officials said they were surprised when German chemicals giant Hoechst released the news at noon (1100 GMT) that it would merge its speciality chemicals business into the Swiss group.
Officials at the Swiss exchange and Clariant said the bourse had been told by Clariant to expect a statement two hours later, at 2:00 p.m. (1300 GMT).
"We were surprised," said Otto Naegeli, member of the Swiss exchange board of directors in charge of market issues.
Naegeli said the incident did not break the bourse's own internal rules on halting trade as soon as important information affecting a share is released.

"It was handled in the correct way. We saw the statement and then we stopped trade," Naegeli told Reuters, adding the bourse could not influence the actions of companies such as Hoechst who were not Swiss Exchange members.
Trade in Clariant was suspended at 12:04 p.m. (1104 GMT) after officials scrambled in response to the Hoechst statement.
In the four minutes of trading before suspension, Clariant shares were still available at between 449 and 460 Swiss francs, as compared to 470 after trade resumed about two hours later.
Clariant registered shares went on to soar 13 percent from the day before to 508 Swiss francs at Tuesday's close and were around 550 at midday on Wednesday.

The prices immediately after the Hoechst announcement triggered as much buying in four minutes as the share usually sees on an average day, around 21,990 shares totalling 10 million francs in 31 deals.
